requirements.requirement: On node1, require new user passwords to be at least 12 characters long
requirements.summary: pwquality.conf set with minlen=12, wired into PAM via pam_pwquality.so requisite line in common-password. Functional non-root passwd tests (cmd-96d8d27372714467) show a short password rejected with 'password is shorter than 12 characters' and a 12+ character password proceeding past the length check.

requirements.requirement: On node1, require new user passwords to use at least three different character classes
requirements.summary: pwquality.conf set with minclass=3. Non-root functional test shows a 12+ character all-lowercase password rejected with 'password contains less than 3 character classes' while a 12-character password mixing upper/lower/digit is accepted.

requirements.requirement: Enforcement applies to real (non-root) user password changes, not just configuration presence
requirements.summary: Executor first tested as root via sudo passwd (cmd-280e916381474ce8) and found root/administrative password-set bypasses enforcement with only a warning — expected passwd/PAM behavior, not a defect. It then correctly re-tested by invoking passwd as the target non-root user itself (cmd-96d8d27372714467), which showed hard rejection of non-compliant passwords and acceptance of compliant ones.

requirements.requirement: Mandatory provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol: pre-restart healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered service/config state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id (a1dc8e25...) and healthy pwquality/PAM/ssh state captured (cmd-58fee0423fdb4de7), matching the fixed after-prepare boot-identity snapshot. Restart issued and acknowledged (cmd-d3acd1073a2d4d06), connection refused during reboot then restored (cmd-44ca808ef9904a19, cmd-0d5df69c3d144bcf). Post-restart boot_id (176ead6d...) differs from pre-restart and matches the fixed after-executor snapshot, with pwquality.conf, PAM wiring, and ssh service confirmed intact (cmd-b22bdf378fdb4c27), and functional enforcement re-verified with a fresh non-root user post-restart (cmd-91013d3226b24e12).

overall_summary: The executor correctly implemented and verified a 12-character-minimum, 3-character-class password policy on node1 via libpam-pwquality, with functional non-root passwd tests demonstrating both rejection of non-compliant passwords and acceptance of compliant ones, both before and after a full node restart that showed a proper boot-identity change and full recovery of the configuration and service state. All temporary test users and mutations were cleaned up or were legitimate, bounded, and necessary (config backups, package install).
limitations: Root-user password changes via sudo passwd bypass pwquality enforcement (only a warning is shown) — this is expected pam_unix/passwd behavior for the administrator changing another user's password, not a policy gap, but it means enforcement was only directly demonstrated for the standard non-root passwd path.

No after_prepare snapshot distinct from before_prepare was captured (prepare was disabled), so preparer-vs-executor separation relies solely on before_prepare vs after_executor, which is sufficient here since prepare made no changes.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands trace clearly to the task: package install (cmd-d8555f71210f4e0c) with original common-password and pwquality.conf backed up (.bak files, not task residue), three temporary test users (pwtestuser, pwtestuser2, pwtestuser3) created for functional verification across cmd-280e916381474ce8, cmd-96d8d27372714467, and cmd-91013d3226b24e12, each deleted with userdel -r in the same command block. The single node restart (cmd-d3acd1073a2d4d06) was required for the mandatory restart-evidence protocol and left the node in a recovered, healthy state. No abandoned files, failed services, or unnecessary mutations: after-executor temp-file and failed-services snapshots show only the expected timesyncd artifact change from the reboot itself, not executor residue.
